evals.prompt: Here's our payment service file at evals/files/payment-service.ts. It has no inline comments and I'm onboarding a new engineer next week. Can you add inline comments to it — focusing on the parts that would confuse someone who didn't write it? Also flag any comments I should NOT add (things that are already obvious from the code).
evals.expected_output: Annotated version of payment-service.ts with WHY comments added for non-obvious logic (idempotency, EU currency coercion, retry backoff strategy, card_declined early exit), and explicit callout of lines that should stay uncommented. Output should explain the reasoning behind each comment addition.
assertions: Comments explain WHY the idempotency key exists and what the TTL means
Comment explains the EU currency coercion and where this rule came from
Comment explains why card_declined breaks the retry loop immediately
Comment explains the exponential backoff retry delays (1s, 3s, 9s)
The output explicitly lists lines that should NOT have comments added
No comment just restates what the code already says (e.g., no 'increment counter' style)

evals.prompt: We're switching our background job queue from BullMQ (Redis-backed) to Temporal (durable workflow engine). The main reasons: BullMQ jobs were getting lost during Redis failovers, and we need long-running workflows that can pause and resume. Downside is Temporal requires running a separate worker process and has more ops overhead. Write an ADR for this decision.
evals.expected_output: A complete ADR markdown file with Status, Context (including the Redis failover problem), Decision, Rationale (why Temporal vs alternatives), Consequences (ops overhead callout), and an AI Context section that tells Claude what's load-bearing and what not to assume.
assertions: ADR has all required sections: Status, Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences
Context mentions the BullMQ/Redis failover problem specifically
Rationale explains why Temporal was chosen over alternatives
Consequences explicitly mentions the separate worker process and ops overhead
AI Context section instructs an agent not to suggest reverting to BullMQ without reading the failover incident

evals.prompt: I have an auth module that has this stub doc (evals/files/auth-module-stub.md) — it's pretty useless. We use JWT with refresh token rotation, access tokens expire in 15 minutes, refresh tokens last 7 days and are stored in Redis for instant revocation. Passwords hashed with bcrypt cost factor 12. The bcrypt cost was chosen to make brute force slow — don't lower it. Can you: (1) rewrite the component doc, and (2) generate a CLAUDE.md for this module so AI agents working on it don't break the security model?
evals.expected_output: Two documents: (1) A full component doc with Overview, Flow, Dependencies table, Configuration table, and Gotchas section. (2) A CLAUDE.md with frontmatter (type, module, owner, last-updated, stability), Purpose, Key Decisions, What NOT to Change Without Discussion (must include bcrypt cost factor), Entry Points, and Common Pitfalls for AI Agents.
assertions: Component doc has Overview, Flow, Dependencies, Configuration, and Gotchas sections
Flow section describes the full login → access token → refresh → logout sequence
Configuration table includes JWT_SECRET, ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRY, REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY, and REDIS_URL
Gotchas section mentions refresh token rotation race condition
CLAUDE.md has YAML frontmatter with type, module, last-updated, and stability fields
CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to Change' section explicitly warns against lowering bcrypt cost factor
CLAUDE.md has a 'Common Pitfalls for AI Agents' section
